## Plan-review rev4 (LLM tier ran) — BLOCK on one G6 finding; resolved in rev5 plan

**Blocking (G6).** "Widening `store_uninitialized` to fire for broken/mid-clone stores collides
with the audit-server consumer, which degrades that exact code to an empty page — silently
blanking a genuinely broken store, the same masking this change exists to remove." Cites
`src/rebar/audit/server.py:101` and `tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py:163`.

**Analysis.** Correct catch. `audit.server._audited_tickets` catches `store_uninitialized` and
degrades to an empty index. Its docstring PROMISES "a genuinely broken store is not silently
blanked" — a promise that held only because broken/mid-clone stores used to read `[]` (never
raised). This fix makes them raise `store_uninitialized`, so they now fall into the caught bucket
and the docstring's guarantee becomes false. (Behavior at the audit layer is actually unchanged —
those stores rendered empty before too — but the module now silently blanks them while claiming it
does not.)

**Resolution (in approved scope — this is the caller-sweep reconciliation the operator asked me to
complete; NOT a new behavior change).** Keep the index rendering empty for any `store_uninitialized`
(a read-only web index must not 500), but make it HONEST and NON-silent: correct the docstring, and
broaden the WARNING log so a present-but-unusable store is logged. Operators diagnose store health
via the driving agent / CLI, which now surfaces the absent-vs-unusable distinction. Added
`src/rebar/audit/server.py` to file_impact and an AUDIT acceptance criterion (renders empty AND
logs for a present-but-unusable store; still propagates a non-`store_uninitialized` failure).

**Advisory folded in (T5b).** `store_is_usable`'s git-subprocess failure taxonomy is now explicit:
`check=False` so a clean non-zero rc == "HEAD unresolvable" -> not usable, while an OSError (git
binary missing / env failure) PROPAGATES rather than collapsing into `store_uninitialized`. Pinned
by a new predicate test.

Description trimmed to <8000 chars (P4). Re-running `review-plan` for a non-BLOCK verdict.
